raw.query: WITH current_runs AS (SELECT run_id FROM provenance.v_dim WHERE is_current = true), encoder AS (SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE n_images = 121) AS rows_at_121, MAX(n_images) FILTER (WHERE is_valid) AS max_tested_n_images, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE raw::text ILIKE '%deepstack%' OR note ILIKE '%deepstack%') AS deepstack_rows FROM provenance.collector_encoder_fn), windows AS (SELECT MAX(images::double precision / NULLIF(n_image_reqs, 0)) AS max_window_mean_images_per_image_request FROM provenance.collector_anchor_window_engine), cost AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS current_cost_rows FROM provenance.v_cost_ratio c JOIN current_runs d USING (run_id) WHERE c.is_current = true) SELECT encoder.rows_at_121, encoder.max_tested_n_images, encoder.deepstack_rows, windows.max_window_mean_images_per_image_request, cost.current_cost_rows, 6.4 * 121 * 8 / 25 AS claimed_transfer_ms_decimal_mb FROM encoder CROSS JOIN windows CROSS JOIN cost
raw.claimed: ≈6.4 MB/image and ≈250 ms at a 121-image maximum
raw.evidence: The 250 ms arithmetic holds conditionally, but the DB has no DeepStack payload row and reports a window mean of 124.17 images per image-bearing request, which cannot coexist with a comparable 121-image maximum.
raw.fix: Back the four tensor sizes explicitly and replace or qualify the 121-image denominator using a comparable per-request maximum, then recompute transfer time.
